_note: County pods: market groupings (same plants, same haul, same bidders) used as a pricing tier between county and district. GARBOYLIN deliberately crosses a KYTC district line -- Lincoln is D08 but its market is with Garrard and Boyle in D07. Do not 'correct' that. Jackson is intentionally absent: it prices on its own, county then district. SEKY and LAURELCLAY were added 2026-08-27 from measured bidder overlap (Jaccard on bidder sets, 2022+): Clay-Laurel 52%, Harlan-Knox 50%, Clay-Jackson 48%, Bell-Knox 47%. LAURELCLAY crosses a district line the same way GARBOYLIN does -- Rockcastle is D08, the rest D11. Jackson is no longer standalone: Jacob approved folding it into LAURELCLAY, which rescues 84 item codes that Jackson alone could not price (48 cells solo vs 264 pooled).
_tables_note: Pod price tables are built from Supabase allen-qc bid_items.low_bid_unit_price joined to bid_projects (county, letting_date), lettings 2022-01-01 onward, pooling the RAW bid rows across a pod's member counties. Every row is normalised to 2025 dollars before the median is taken -- non-asphalt by the ESC 'other' chain, asphalt by stripping binder at that year's KAPI, escalating the residual on the asphalt chain, and re-adding binder at the 2025 KAPI -- so yr is 2025 for every cell and the tier is consistent with geo.district. Requires n>=3. Lump-sum ratio codes are excluded (priced as a percent of the work subtotal elsewhere). Cells are dropped when the median is below $0.05 or outside 0.25x-4x the newest statewide average, which removes penny bids from unbalanced bidding. Low bid runs a measured 0.5% under the all-bidder average (median ratio 0.9953 over 2,324 multi-bidder lines), so it is effectively unbiased against the AUBP averages the district tables use. The three August 2026 holdout jobs are NOT in this database -- verified, no leakage.
